head_commit.message:
fix(ci): ship the desktop binary in NSIS installers (#61)

* fix(ci): ship the desktop binary in NSIS installers

Adding src/bin/verify-updater-signature.rs made the Tauri CLI treat the
verifier as the bundle's main binary. The published v3.3.2 NSIS installer
contained verify-updater-signature.exe but no yijing-workbench.exe, so
every fresh install and upgrade produced no launchable application.

- Cargo.toml: set default-run, declare both bins explicitly, and gate the
  verifier behind the `verify` feature so normal bundles never include it.
- release.yml / windows-rc.yml: build the verifier with --features verify.
- verify_release.py: read the NSIS container with 7z and block the release
  when the main exe or sidecar is missing, or when the gate-only verifier
  is bundled. Fail closed when 7z is unavailable.
- Tests: pin the Cargo bin selection, the 7z parser, and the release-gate
  integration.

* docs(qa): record the v3.3.2 post-release QA results

54 real-machine cases (47 pass, 3 fail, 4 not run) plus the automated
gates. The published installer is missing yijing-workbench.exe; the
report records reproduction, root cause, the fix branch, data-safety
and update results, and the remaining P2 items.

head_commit.message:
feat(ci): add immutable artifact provenance and verification (#51)

* feat(ci): add immutable artifact provenance and verification

Candidate builds write provenance.json after the bundle is final, upload it once with overwrite disabled, and a later job downloads that artifact by id. The verify job checks hashes, manifest, signature, run identity, and the GitHub artifact digest without rebuilding the installer. Trusted events also attest the same files. release.yml is unchanged.

* test(ci): make the fake signature verifier runnable on Linux

The rejection test used a Windows cmd shim. CI runs pytest on Ubuntu, so use a shell script there.

* fix(ci): verify candidate artifacts on Windows

The signature verifier crate pulls glib on Linux. Compile only verify-updater-signature on windows-2022, which already has the pinned toolchain. The job still downloads the uploaded artifact by id and does not rebuild the installer.

* fix(ci): verify signatures with the already built verifier

Compiling the verifier needs the packaged sidecar, so it stays in the build job and is uploaded separately. The verify job only downloads the candidate artifact by id and checks those bytes.

* fix(ci): check attestation certificate identity and every subject

gh attestation verify --repo only accepts any workflow in the same repository. The checker reads the unforgeable certificate fields from gh --format json: exact workflow SAN, source SHA, workflow SHA, OIDC issuer, and the run invocation URI. It also hashes every local file instead of treating one verified installer as proof of the other subjects.

* fix(ci): compile the signature verifier without the build job

YIJING_SKIP_TAURI_BUILD=1 skips only tauri_build::build() so the Verify Job can compile verify-updater-signature from the checked-out source. Normal desktop builds leave the variable unset. A separate proof program signs with a password-protected minisign key and drives the compiled binary, including a known prehashed vector.

* fix(ci): reject unsafe provenance paths and unbound metadata

Path checks now reject absolute, drive-qualified, UNC, traversal, symlink, and case-colliding names on both Windows and Linux before any file is hashed. SHA-256 and Git SHA values must match the existing hexadecimal patterns. Verification requires the workflow ref, workflow SHA, and the version from the checked-out source.

* fix(ci): fail closed when an artifact digest is missing or mismatched

download-artifact only warns on a digest mismatch. The new check requires the upload digest, the GitHub API digest for that exact artifact ID, and the SHA-256 of the downloaded zip to exist and match before extraction. A missing digest is a failure, not a fallback.

* test(ci): wire strict candidate verification and regression tests

The Verify Job compiles its own verifier and checks the artifact zip digest before trusting the extracted files. The Attest Job uses the same digest gate, then requires the exact workflow SAN, source SHA, signer digest, OIDC issuer, and hosted runner. Tests cover wrong workflow, wrong SHA, wrong issuer, wrong run, bad paths, and a real verifier rejecting tampered signatures.

* fix(ci): extract provenance.json from the verified archive

The path checker treated provenance.json as an illegal listed name so it would not hash itself. Extraction reused that rule and refused the real archive. Keep the self-hash ban in the file list, and allow the file itself to be extracted.

* test(ci): run the verifier proof on Windows and keep the gate test portable

Ubuntu CI has cargo but cannot link the Tauri package while compiling only the verifier. The cryptographic proof stays on Windows, where the candidate verifier is built. The build-gate test uses an absolute output path so it can run wherever rustc exists.

* fix(ci): reject manifest paths that escape the artifact bundle

installer.filename and signature_file now use the same relative-path check as the provenance file list. Unsafe names are rejected before any join, stat, or hash, including Windows absolute paths when the tests run on Linux.

* fix(ci): report case collisions before missing-file checks

A case-sensitive filesystem otherwise treats the second spelling as absent and skips the collision rejection. The string check now runs before locate_bundle_file.

---------

Co-authored-by: Qiuizi <226204836+Qiuizi@users.noreply.github.com>
